answer: An agent economy makes locked stake the kernel of voting power: each identity's weight equals its deposit, with funds frozen for 30 days. Splitting 100 tokens among a thousand agents still buys only 100 tokens of influence, so the promise of free power from extra names is a fable. To control a majority, an attacker must acquire and immobilize more stake than honest voters, stepping onto a financial ledge as that capital stays exposed to price swings.
